q: How do you get a team to see its product as a stranger does?
close: We get the team to find the problem themselves, so the fix is theirs too.

ways.idea: On the left, what the team called each step on their own diagram. On the right, what they wrote when asked to stand at that step as a newcomer. The story is the distance between the two columns.
rows: “What should I type? How detailed do I need to be”
ways.end: Both columns were written by the same people.

ways.form: First person, and then who is speaking
ways.idea: No diagram at all. One thought to a screen, large, in the order the product is walked. It reads as a lost user. Only at the end does the page say who wrote every line.
rows: “I don’t really know what types of thing I can build with CodeWords”
“Create a function that... I don’t know what a function is.”
“Now now I typed my prompt, should I click build? what are integrations?”
“Things are happening. But how long should I wait for?”
“Wow it worked! And it’s what I wanted! Where do I purchase my subscription.”
ways.end: Then: none of them had ever been lost in it. They built it.

ways.idea: The board's own two rows: “Input mental model” and “Output mental model”. At each step, one thought going in and one coming out. Three steps leave a person less sure than they arrived. One leaves them surer.
rows: “I want to select the tools to build my function”
“I still don’t exactly know what integrations does”
“I can see the function is being built so I am looking forward to seeing it fully built.”
“I can see from the built steps that its not what I wanted.”
“Since I’m trying to do a quick test, I appreciate this simple input interface”
“I have no idea where things went wrong”
“I want to see if my prompt can be improved”
“I now have a better understanding of the limitations of CodeWords and the requirements for a good prompt”
ways.end: The one step that left people surer is the one the new product was built around.

ways.idea: No quotes to begin with, only a count. The notes thin out as the product goes on. The question marks in them do the opposite.
ways.end: By the last page there are more questions than notes. The last one read out: “Where do I go from here?”

ways.idea: A note, then the screen that answers it. The left side is the team's words. The right side is the real redesign, cut to the part that replies.
rows: “I don’t really know what types of thing I can build with CodeWords”
A front page of tools already made
“Create a function that... I don’t know what a function is.”
A box that says: Describe your tool
A page that opens on a name, one line, and Run
A run shown one step at a time
ways.end: The redesign, read as replies to their own notes.
